description: Build a scalable content architecture in the pure logic layer that supports age levels (4-6 = EARLY, 7-10 = LATE), thematic categories, staged/unlockable vocabulary, and English phrases and simple sentences with bidirectional EN<->PL translation and listen-recognition metadata. Expand every module (Colors: shades/more colors/mixing/find-a-color; Letters: uppercase/lowercase pairing, letters-in-words, simple syllables; Numbers: counting, simple picture add/subtract, number ordering). Keep the existing item shape and itemsFor(module) fully backward-compatible so current lessons and progress under naukaweb.v1 keep working. Deliver a solid representative starter set (aim for a few hundred items total, NOT 2000) with a documented, easily extensible format so vocabulary can be grown toward ~2000 later. All work is DOM-free pure logic plus Vitest tests. Depends on FEAT-001.
steps: In docs/js/logic/models.js add age-level constants without breaking existing exports, e.g. export const AGE_LEVELS = Object.freeze({ EARLY: 'EARLY', LATE: 'LATE' }) with a documented mapping (EARLY = ages 4-6, LATE = ages 7-10). Optionally add a helper levelForAge(age) returning EARLY for <=6 else LATE. Keep LEARNING_MODULES and LEITNER unchanged.

Extend docs/js/logic/content.js item builders to accept OPTIONAL new metadata while preserving current fields (id, moduleType, prompt, answer, emoji, colorHex, exampleWord, audioKey). Add optional fields: level (AGE_LEVELS value or array of levels the item is appropriate for; default treat items as available to both if unset so existing items keep working), category (string, e.g. 'animals','food','family','body','clothes','house','nature','transport','verbs','adjectives','colors','numbers','greetings','phrases'), stage (integer >=1 for staged unlock ordering), and for English: kind ('word'|'phrase'|'sentence') and direction support (both EN->PL and PL->EN derivable from prompt/answer). Do NOT remove or rename any existing exported array (colors, polishLetters, numbers, englishWords) or change existing item ids/audioKey schemes.

Greatly expand englishWords into categorized, staged, leveled content: add a substantial representative set across the required categories (animals, colors, numbers, family, food, body, clothes, house, nature, transport, verbs/actions, adjectives), plus simple greetings/phrases (e.g. 'Hello', 'How are you?', 'Thank you', 'Please', 'Good morning') and a set of simple sentences appropriate to LATE level (e.g. 'The cat is black.', 'I have a red ball.'). Tag each with category, stage, level, and kind. Aim for a few hundred English items total (e.g. ~200-350), NOT 2000. Keep every existing english_* id present so stored progress still resolves.

Expand Colors: add more colors and shades (e.g. lighter/darker variants with distinct ids and hex), and add data supporting a 'mixing' concept (e.g. pairs like czerwony+żółty -> pomarańczowy expressed as pure data) and 'find a color in a scene' data (a small set of scene descriptors with a target color). Keep the original 10 color ids unchanged.

Expand Letters: keep all 32 letter ids; add optional lowercase/uppercase pairing data (each letter already has prompt as the uppercase char - add derivable lowercase), data to support letters-in-words recognition (reuse exampleWord, mark the target letter position/highlight index), and simple syllable data for a starter set of Polish words (syllable arrays like ['ko','tek']).

Expand Numbers: keep 0-9 ids; add data supporting counting objects, simple picture-based addition/subtraction problems (pure data: operandA, operandB, operator, result, all small enough for the age band), and number-ordering sequences (arrays of digits to order).

Add pure selector/query helpers in content.js (DOM-free) such as: itemsForLevel(module, level), categoriesFor(module), itemsForCategory(module, category), stagesFor(module), itemsUpToStage(module, stage, level), and englishByKind(kind). These must be deterministic and testable. itemsFor(module) must keep returning the same-or-superset such that existing behavior is preserved (document clearly if it now returns the superset including new items; if that risks changing existing lesson difficulty unexpectedly, keep itemsFor(module) returning the base set and expose expanded content via the new leveled/staged helpers - choose the approach that preserves backward compatibility and document the decision in findings).

Add a clear top-of-file documentation comment in content.js describing the data format and EXACTLY how to add more vocabulary (fields, categories, stages, levels, kinds) to scale toward ~2000 words in later batches.

Add Vitest tests in tests/content.test.js covering: all existing ids still present (colors 10, polishLetters 32, numbers 0-9, and every original english_* id); new helpers return correctly filtered/ordered results (by level, category, stage, kind); staged unlocking is monotonic (itemsUpToStage(module, n) is a superset of itemsUpToStage(module, n-1)); English has word/phrase/sentence kinds and both translation directions are derivable; expanded color/letter/number data structures have the expected fields.
Run `npm test` and confirm all tests (old + new) pass.
acceptance_criteria: All existing content ids remain present and unchanged (colors 10, letters 32, numbers 0-9, all original english_* ids).
content.js exposes leveled/categorized/staged query helpers that are pure and deterministic.

English content includes categorized vocabulary across the required categories plus greetings/phrases and simple sentences, tagged with level/category/stage/kind, totaling a few hundred items (not 2000).
Colors, Letters, and Numbers have expanded pure data supporting the new sub-topics (shades/mixing/find-color; uppercase-lowercase/letters-in-words/syllables; counting/add-subtract/ordering).
content.js has a documentation comment explaining how to add vocabulary toward ~2000.
`npm test` passes including new tests/content.test.js; existing 35 tests still pass.
findings: Pure-logic-only feature; no UI/DOM changes. models.js: added AGE_LEVELS {EARLY,LATE} and levelForAge(age) (<=6 EARLY else LATE); LEARNING_MODULES and LEITNER untouched. content.js rewritten additively: builders now take optional opts {level,category,stage,kind,id} via a withMeta() merge; the english() builder supports an explicit opts.id for phrases/sentences (audioKey derived from the id) while plain words keep the english_<word> scheme. All original ids preserved and verified by tests (10 colors as first entries, 32 letters, numbers 0-9, all 24 original english_* ids present). itemsFor(module) DECISION: it now returns the full exported superset for every module (colors 20, englishWords 140) rather than the base set. Rationale: the existing lessonView.itemsFor(module) only picks a random QUESTIONS_PER_LESSON chunk, so difficulty is not pinned to a fixed item set, and progressService uses itemsFor(module).length only for total-per-module badge math. Consequence to note: module-master badges (color_master needs all 20 colors, English polyglot/mastery spans 140) now require more mastered items; gamification tests use explicit counts, not the catalog, so all pass. New pure helpers added: itemsForLevel, categoriesFor, itemsForCategory, stagesFor, itemsUpToStage (monotonic supersets, optional level filter), englishByKind, translationPair (derives EN->PL and PL->EN from a single item). English starter set = 140 items across 15 categories (animals, colors, numbers, family, food, body, clothes, house, nature, transport, verbs, adjectives, greetings, phrases, sentences), stages 1-5, with word/phrase/sentence kinds; sentences are all LATE. Colors expanded to 20 + colorMixes + colorScenes data. Letters: letterCasePairs, lettersInWords (target index into exampleWord), syllableWords. Numbers: countingTasks, mathProblems (result within 0-9), orderingSequences. Top-of-file doc comment documents the data format and exactly how to scale toward ~2000 words. Tests: added tests/content.test.js (30 tests). npm test => 65 passed (35 existing + 30 new).
